items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'line manager'?
options: A specialist role that gives advice and support to line managers but has no direct authority over the line employees, e.g. legal or HR advisers.
A manager with direct authority over subordinates in the chain of command, responsible for their performance.
The number of subordinates who report directly to one manager or supervisor.
Removing one or more levels of the management hierarchy, which usually widens spans of control.
items.answer: A manager with direct authority over subordinates in the chain of command, responsible for their performance.
items.markingKey: line manager: A manager with direct authority over subordinates in the chain of command, responsible for their performance.

items.stem: According to Porter, a firm that targets a narrow segment with a unique product is following
options: a differentiation focus strategy
a mass market strategy
a cost leadership strategy
a cost focus strategy
items.answer: a differentiation focus strategy
items.markingKey: a differentiation focus strategy. Focus = narrow target; differentiation focus = unique product for a niche.

items.stem: Based in Auckland, Kiwi Trails Ltd (private limited company) runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. The business has around 90 employees. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Explain one disadvantage to Kiwi Trails of financing its expansion with a large long-term loan.
items.answer: Higher gearing and financial risk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. higher gearing and financial risk; interest must be paid even if profits fall; lenders may impose conditions. 1 mark: explained in the context of Kiwi Trails (tourism). [2]

items.stem: Pearl Logistics WLL sells a product in Qatar for $65.00. A similar imported product sells for $50. The government imposes a 20% tariff on imports, which is passed on in full. Calculate the new price of the imported product and the price difference between the two products.
items.answer: $60.00; difference $5.00
items.markingKey: Import price = $50 × 1.20 = $60.00 [1]; difference = $5.00 (import still cheaper) [1]. [2]

items.stem: Mekong Furniture JSC is a joint stock company based in Hanoi, Vietnam. It makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe and employs about 1,200 people. A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. Analyse how Porter's five forces could help Mekong Furniture understand the competitive pressures in its industry.
items.answer: Points to develop for Mekong Furniture: five forces analyse industry competition; buyer and supplier power affect prices and margins; threat of entrants and substitutes limits pricing; rivalry determines intensity of competition.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: five forces analyse industry competition. AO2 Application [2]: answer uses the case (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Mekong Furniture, e.g. buyer and supplier power affect prices and margins; threat of entrants and substitutes limits pricing; rivalry determines intensity of competition. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [6]

items.stem: A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Nusantara Apparel Tbk, a public limited company in Indonesia with about 4,000 employees, makes sportswear under contract for global brands. Discuss the usefulness of the income statement in judging the performance of Nusantara Apparel.
items.answer: For: shows profitability and margins; trends over time; comparisons with rivals. Against: profit is not cash; historic data; ignores non-financial performance. Judgement: the decision for Nusantara Apparel depends mainly on the quality of profit, and also on the use of other statements.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Nusantara Apparel: clothing manufacturing, about 4,000 employees, public limited company in Indonesia; a global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. shows profitability and margins; trends over time; comparisons with rivals; arguments against, e.g. profit is not cash; historic data; ignores non-financial performance. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the quality of profit; the use of other statements; comparability of data. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Nusantara Apparel, not a generic one. [8]

items.stem: Nile Pharma plc is a public limited company based in Cairo, Egypt. It manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East and employs about 1,800 people. Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. Evaluate whether Nile Pharma should stop producing a product that shows a loss under full costing.
items.answer: For: loss-making on full cost; resources could go to more profitable lines; simpler range. Against: positive contribution helps pay fixed costs; complementary sales may be lost; fixed costs remain after closure. Judgement: the decision for Nile Pharma depends mainly on the contribution of the product, and also on alternative uses of capacity.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Nile Pharma: pharmaceuticals, about 1,800 employees, public limited company in Egypt; most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. loss-making on full cost; resources could go to more profitable lines; simpler range; arguments against, e.g. positive contribution helps pay fixed costs; complementary sales may be lost; fixed costs remain after closure. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the contribution of the product; alternative uses of capacity; effect on customers and brand. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Nile Pharma, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'opportunity cost'?
options: Costs that cannot be traced directly to a particular product or cost centre, such as rent, insurance and management salaries.
A costing method in which all indirect costs (overheads) are allocated to products or cost centres, so each product bears a share of total costs.
The benefit of the next best alternative that is given up when a decision is made.
A one-off order from a customer, often at a lower price than normal, which the business must decide whether to accept.
items.answer: The benefit of the next best alternative that is given up when a decision is made.
items.markingKey: opportunity cost: The benefit of the next best alternative that is given up when a decision is made.

items.stem: Which is an example of industrial action short of a strike?
options: A lock-out by the employer
A no-strike agreement
A work-to-rule
Arbitration
items.answer: A work-to-rule
items.markingKey: A work-to-rule. Work-to-rule, go-slows and overtime bans are action short of a strike.

items.stem: IslaConnect Inc. is a private limited company based in Manila, the Philippines. It runs customer-service call centres for banks and airlines in the USA and Australia and employs about 2,600 people. Clients are starting to replace human call handlers with artificial intelligence. Explain one disadvantage to IslaConnect of introducing total quality management.
items.answer: High training costs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. high training costs; culture change takes years; staff and managers may resist. 1 mark: explained in the context of IslaConnect (business process outsourcing). [2]

items.stem: Pearl Logistics WLL is considering an ERP system costing $800,000. It is expected to cut inventory holding costs by $100,000 a year and administration labour costs by $100,000 a year, with running costs of $20,000 a year. Calculate the net annual saving and the payback period.
items.answer: $180,000 a year; payback 4.44 years

items.stem: Based in Istanbul, Bosphorus Home AŞ (public limited company) makes washing machines, fridges and ovens sold in Europe and the Middle East. The business has around 3,500 employees. Inflation in Turkey has been above 40% for two years. Analyse how an increase in gearing could affect Bosphorus Home and its shareholders.
items.answer: Points to develop for Bosphorus Home: gearing = NCL ÷ capital employed; higher interest costs and financial risk; possible higher returns on equity if investment succeeds; harder to borrow more in future.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: gearing = NCL ÷ capital employed. AO2 Application [2]: answer uses the case (Bosphorus Home: household appliance manufacturing, about 3,500 employees, public limited company in Turkey; inflation in Turkey has been above 40% for two years). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Bosphorus Home, e.g. higher interest costs and financial risk; possible higher returns on equity if investment succeeds; harder to borrow more in future. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [6]

items.stem: Based in Bogotá, Café Cordillera SAS (private limited company) roasts coffee and runs a chain of 60 cafés. The business has around 900 employees. The owners want to double the number of cafés within three years. Discuss whether Café Cordillera should always choose the option with the highest expected value.
items.answer: For: maximises long-run average return; objective; easy to compare. Against: risk of large loss; estimates may be wrong; qualitative and ethical factors. Judgement: the decision for Café Cordillera depends mainly on the size of the possible loss relative to its finance, and also on confidence in probabilities.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Café Cordillera: food and drink retail, about 900 employees, private limited company in Colombia; the owners want to double the number of cafés within three years). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. maximises long-run average return; objective; easy to compare; arguments against, e.g. risk of large loss; estimates may be wrong; qualitative and ethical factors. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the size of the possible loss relative to its finance; confidence in probabilities; strategic fit. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Café Cordillera, not a generic one. [8]

items.stem: Based in Kuala Lumpur, BatikPay Sdn Bhd (private limited company) runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. The business has around 210 employees. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Evaluate the most important factor in successfully managing change at BatikPay.
items.answer: For: leadership and vision; communication; involvement of staff. Against: resources and training also needed; culture may block change; external pressures. Judgement: the decision for BatikPay depends mainly on the scale of the change, and also on the current culture.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (BatikPay: financial technology, about 210 employees, private limited company in Malaysia; the central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. leadership and vision; communication; involvement of staff; arguments against, e.g. resources and training also needed; culture may block change; external pressures. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the scale of the change; the current culture; trust between managers and staff. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to BatikPay, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'PESTLE analysis'?
options: An analysis of the political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental factors in a business's external environment.
A strategic analysis tool that identifies a business's internal strengths and weaknesses and the external opportunities and threats it faces.
A model that classifies a firm's products or business units by market growth rate and relative market share into stars, cash cows, question marks (problem children) and dogs.
A feature or capability that allows a business to outperform its rivals, by offering better value through lower prices or greater benefits.
items.answer: An analysis of the political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental factors in a business's external environment.
items.markingKey: PESTLE analysis: An analysis of the political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental factors in a business's external environment.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'unique selling point (USP)'?
options: The scientific and technical work carried out to create new products and processes or improve existing ones.
Allowing a business in another country to use the brand name, products and methods in return for a fee and royalty.
A legal right that gives the inventor of a new product or process the sole right to make, use and sell it for a set period.
A feature of a product or brand that customers value and that distinguishes it from all competitors.
items.answer: A feature of a product or brand that customers value and that distinguishes it from all competitors.
items.markingKey: unique selling point (USP): A feature of a product or brand that customers value and that distinguishes it from all competitors.

items.stem: Based in Cairo, Nile Pharma plc (public limited company) manufactures generic medicines for hospitals and pharmacies in Africa and the Middle East. The business has around 1,800 employees. Most of its raw ingredients are imported and paid for in US dollars. Explain one advantage to Nile Pharma of increasing globalisation of its industry.
items.answer: Larger export markets for generic medicines.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. larger export markets for generic medicines; access to cheaper global suppliers; economies of scale from selling worldwide. 1 mark: explained in the context of Nile Pharma (pharmaceuticals). [2]

items.stem: A project has these activities: A (12 days, starts at once); B (4 days, after A); C (11 days, after B); D (4 days, after A); E (7 days, after D); F (2 days, after C and E); G (12 days, after F). Calculate the earliest start time of every activity and the minimum project duration.
items.answer: A 0, B 12, C 16, D 12, E 16, F 27, G 29; duration 41 days
items.markingKey: EST = latest of (EST + duration) of preceding activities: A=0, B=12, C=16, D=12, E=16, F=27, G=29 [1]; duration = 41 days [1]. [2]

items.stem: Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Pearl Logistics WLL, a private limited company in Qatar with about 1,500 employees, provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. Analyse how introducing TQM could improve the competitiveness of Pearl Logistics.
items.answer: Points to develop for Pearl Logistics: TQM makes quality everyone's responsibility; fewer defects lower costs of freight and warehousing services; improved reputation and customer loyalty; motivated staff through involvement.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: TQM makes quality everyone's responsibility. AO2 Application [2]: answer uses the case (Pearl Logistics: logistics, about 1,500 employees, private limited company in Qatar; large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Pearl Logistics, e.g. fewer defects lower costs of freight and warehousing services; improved reputation and customer loyalty; motivated staff through involvement. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [6]

items.stem: Based in Bangkok, Siam Ready Meals Co. Ltd (private limited company) produces chilled and frozen ready meals for supermarkets and convenience stores. The business has around 1,100 employees. Its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day. (a) Define 'business plan'. (b) Analyse how a corporate plan could help Siam Ready Meals achieve its long-term objectives.
items.answer: (a) A document describing a business, its objectives and strategies, the market it operates in and its financial forecasts, often used to obtain finance. (b) Corporate plan sets objectives, strategies and resources; coordinates functional plans; allocates finance to priorities; allows monitoring and review.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) AO1 Knowledge [2]: corporate plan sets objectives, strategies and resources. AO2 Application [2]: answer uses the case (Siam Ready Meals: food manufacturing, about 1,100 employees, private limited company in Thailand; its biggest customer, a convenience-store chain, wants deliveries twice a day). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Siam Ready Meals, e.g. coordinates functional plans; allocates finance to priorities; allows monitoring and review. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [6]

items.stem: Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Kiwi Trails Ltd, a private limited company in New Zealand with about 90 employees, runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. Discuss whether big data will replace traditional market research for businesses such as Kiwi Trails.
items.answer: For: huge volumes of real behaviour data; faster and continuous; cheaper per insight once systems exist. Against: shows what but not why customers act; new products lack data; qualitative research gives depth. Judgement: the decision for Kiwi Trails depends mainly on the type of decision, and also on the cost of each method.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Kiwi Trails: tourism, about 90 employees, private limited company in New Zealand; bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer). AO3 Analysis [4]: arguments for, e.g. huge volumes of real behaviour data; faster and continuous; cheaper per insight once systems exist; arguments against, e.g. shows what but not why customers act; new products lack data; qualitative research gives depth. AO4 Evaluation [4]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the type of decision; the cost of each method; the availability of data in its market. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Kiwi Trails, not a generic one. [12]

items.stem: What is the main purpose of contingency planning?
options: To be ready to respond quickly to unexpected events
To increase short-term profit
To guarantee no crisis will happen
To replace the corporate plan
items.answer: To be ready to respond quickly to unexpected events
items.markingKey: To be ready to respond quickly to unexpected events. Plans reduce the damage and response time when events occur.

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'tariff'?
options: Reductions in average cost that a firm gains from the growth of its whole industry or area, e.g. a pool of skilled labour or specialist suppliers nearby.
A tax on imported goods, which raises their price in the domestic market.
A merger or takeover with a firm at a different stage of production in the same industry, either backward (towards suppliers) or forward (towards customers).
The prices one part of a multinational charges another part in a different country, which can be set to shift profits to low-tax countries.
items.answer: A tax on imported goods, which raises their price in the domestic market.
items.markingKey: tariff: A tax on imported goods, which raises their price in the domestic market.

items.stem: Based in Seoul, Han River Games Co. (private limited company) develops mobile games that earn revenue from in-game purchases. The business has around 340 employees. One game earns 70% of its revenue and its popularity is starting to fall. Explain one disadvantage to Han River Games of using decision trees to choose between strategic options.
items.answer: Probabilities are estimates.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. probabilities are estimates; ignores qualitative factors; expected value is an average not an actual outcome. 1 mark: explained in the context of Han River Games (video game development). [2]

items.stem: Annual sales in a market are: Café Cordillera $145m, Lumen Robotics $130m, BatikPay $60m, Desert Bloom $45m, Gold Coast Cocoa $35m; all other firms $200m. Calculate the three-firm concentration ratio.

Based in Santiago, Andina Solar SpA (private limited company) designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. The business has around 380 employees. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Analyse the benefits to Andina Solar of moving from quality control to quality assurance.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andina Solar: QA prevents faults at every stage; lower waste and inspection costs; empowered staff are more motivated; more consistent quality of solar installations.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: QA prevents faults at every stage. AO2 Application [2]: answer uses the case (Andina Solar: renewable energy, about 380 employees, private limited company in Chile; the government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Andina Solar, e.g. lower waste and inspection costs; empowered staff are more motivated; more consistent quality of solar installations. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [6]

items.stem: Based in Muscat, Muscat Dates & Co. LLC (family-owned limited company) processes, packs and exports dates and date syrup. The business has around 160 employees. Three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor. Recommend the most suitable method for Muscat Dates to enter the market in Europe.
items.answer: For: exporting is low risk; joint venture brings local knowledge; own subsidiary gives control. Against: exporting faces tariffs and transport costs; joint ventures share profits; subsidiaries need large investment. Judgement: the decision for Muscat Dates depends mainly on its resources and experience, and also on the size and risk of the market.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Muscat Dates: food processing, about 160 employees, family-owned limited company in Oman; three family members disagree about whether to sell shares to an outside investor). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. exporting is low risk; joint venture brings local knowledge; own subsidiary gives control; arguments against, e.g. exporting faces tariffs and transport costs; joint ventures share profits; subsidiaries need large investment. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its resources and experience; the size and risk of the market; trade barriers. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Muscat Dates, not a generic one. [8]

items.stem: Mekong Furniture JSC is a joint stock company based in Hanoi, Vietnam. It makes wooden and rattan furniture for large retailers in the USA and Europe and employs about 1,200 people. A major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six. (a) Define 'strategic management'. (b) Evaluate the most important source of competitive advantage for Mekong Furniture.
items.answer: (a) The process of analysing the business and its environment, choosing a strategy and implementing and reviewing it to achieve long-term objectives. (b) For: low costs; brand and reputation; innovation and core competencies. Against: costs can be matched by rivals; brands take time and money; innovation can be copied. Judgement: the decision for Mekong Furniture depends mainly on the nature of its market, and also on its resources and capabilities.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Mekong Furniture: furniture manufacturing, about 1,200 employees, joint stock company in Vietnam; a major US retailer has asked it to cut delivery times from twelve weeks to six). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. low costs; brand and reputation; innovation and core competencies; arguments against, e.g. costs can be matched by rivals; brands take time and money; innovation can be copied. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the nature of its market; its resources and capabilities; what customers value most. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Mekong Furniture, not a generic one. [10]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'delayering'?
options: The route through which authority passes down and communication passes up and down an organisation.
Removing one or more levels of the management hierarchy, which usually widens spans of control.
The official structure of roles, reporting lines and communication channels set out in the organisation chart.
Keeping decision-making authority at the top of the organisation or at head office.
items.answer: Removing one or more levels of the management hierarchy, which usually widens spans of control.
items.markingKey: delayering: Removing one or more levels of the management hierarchy, which usually widens spans of control.

items.stem: Which business term is described here: "Reductions in average cost that a firm gains from the growth of its whole industry or area, e.g. a pool of skilled labour or specialist suppliers nearby."
options: external economies of scale
trade bloc
vertical integration
globalisation
items.answer: external economies of scale
items.markingKey: This is the definition of external economies of scale.

items.stem: Andes Textil SA is a family-owned private company based in Lima, Peru. It makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan and employs about 320 people. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Explain one disadvantage to Andes Textil of retaining most of its profit for the year rather than paying dividends.
items.answer: Shareholders may be dissatisfied.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant disadvantage, e.g. shareholders may be dissatisfied; share price may fall; opportunity cost of the funds. 1 mark: explained in the context of Andes Textil (textile manufacturing). [1]

items.stem: Kiwi Trails Ltd is considering introducing automation in its main factory. Managers score each force from 1 (weak) to 5 (strong): driving forces — government grants 5, cost savings 5, pressure from competitors 5; restraining forces — cost of change 5, lack of skills 3, employee resistance 3. Calculate the total of each set of forces and state what the analysis suggests.
items.answer: Driving 15, restraining 11: change favoured
items.markingKey: Driving = 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 [1]; restraining = 5 + 3 + 3 = 11 [1]; drivers exceed restrainers, so change likely to succeed [1]. [3]

items.stem: Andes Textil SA is a family-owned private company based in Lima, Peru. It makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan and employs about 320 people. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Analyse why a business plan would be important if Andes Textil sought outside finance to launch a range of alpaca home furnishings.
items.answer: Points to develop for Andes Textil: business plan sets out objectives and forecasts; investors and banks assess risk and return; shows market research and strategy; cash-flow forecasts show ability to repay.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: business plan sets out objectives and forecasts. AO2 Application [2]: answer uses the case (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [2]: developed chains of reasoning showing the consequence for Andes Textil, e.g. investors and banks assess risk and return; shows market research and strategy; cash-flow forecasts show ability to repay. Levels: L1 knowledge only; L2 applied to the case; L3 applied and analysed. [6]

items.stem: Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd, a private limited company in South Africa with about 140 employees, brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets. Discuss the importance of quality to the competitiveness of Cape Brew.
items.answer: For: reputation and loyalty; premium pricing; lower costs of waste. Against: price may matter more to customers; improving quality is costly; other factors such as delivery speed. Judgement: the decision for Cape Brew depends mainly on its market positioning, and also on what competitors offer.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Cape Brew: beverages, about 140 employees, private limited company in South Africa; demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. reputation and loyalty; premium pricing; lower costs of waste; arguments against, e.g. price may matter more to customers; improving quality is costly; other factors such as delivery speed. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on its market positioning; what competitors offer; the cost of quality failures. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Cape Brew, not a generic one. [8]

items.stem: Pearl Logistics WLL is a private limited company based in Doha, Qatar. It provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services and employs about 1,500 people. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. (a) Define 'monetary policy'. (b) Discuss the extent to which government economic policies in Qatar are likely to affect the success of Pearl Logistics.
items.answer: (a) Decisions by the central bank on interest rates and the money supply, used mainly to control inflation. (b) For: interest rates affect borrowing costs and demand; tax changes affect prices and profits; supply-side policies affect skills and costs. Against: internal factors such as management and products matter more; competition and global demand may dominate; policies may change before they have effect. Judgement: the decision for Pearl Logistics depends mainly on how much it borrows and exports, and also on the size and timing of policy changes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark partial, 2 marks full definition [2] (b) AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Pearl Logistics: logistics, about 1,500 employees, private limited company in Qatar; large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. interest rates affect borrowing costs and demand; tax changes affect prices and profits; supply-side policies affect skills and costs; arguments against, e.g. internal factors such as management and products matter more; competition and global demand may dominate; policies may change before they have effect. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how much it borrows and exports; the size and timing of policy changes; the quality of its strategy. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Pearl Logistics, not a generic one. [10]

items.stem: Which of the following best defines 'time value of money'?
options: The possibility that the actual results of an investment differ from those forecast, especially that returns are lower.
Testing how the outcome of an investment appraisal changes if key forecasts (e.g. sales, costs, discount rate) turn out differently.
Reducing the value of future cash flows to give their present value, because money received in the future is worth less than money received today.
The idea that a sum of money is worth more now than the same sum in the future, because it could be invested to earn interest.
items.answer: The idea that a sum of money is worth more now than the same sum in the future, because it could be invested to earn interest.
items.markingKey: time value of money: The idea that a sum of money is worth more now than the same sum in the future, because it could be invested to earn interest.

items.stem: A business starts selling its existing products in a new country. This is
options: market development
diversification
product development
market penetration
items.answer: market development
items.markingKey: market development. Existing product, new market.

items.stem: Based in Santiago, Andina Solar SpA (private limited company) designs and installs solar power systems for farms, mines and homes. The business has around 380 employees. The government has announced new subsidies for business investment in renewable energy. Explain one advantage to Andina Solar of introducing zero budgeting.
items.answer: Every item of spending is justified.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. every item of spending is justified; removes waste and outdated spending; resources move to priority areas. 1 mark: explained in the context of Andina Solar (renewable energy). [1]

items.stem: Desert Bloom Hotels plc is a public limited company based in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates. It operates fourteen four- and five-star hotels and employs about 3,100 people. Occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby. Explain how the managers of Desert Bloom could use ratio analysis to improve decision-making.
items.answer: Points to develop for Desert Bloom: ratios measure profitability, liquidity, efficiency, gearing; trends identify problems early; inter-firm comparison benchmarks performance; sets targets for departments.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: ratios measure profitability, liquidity, efficiency, gearing. AO2 Application [1]: answer uses the case (Desert Bloom: hospitality, about 3,100 employees, public limited company in the United Arab Emirates; occupancy rates have fallen since two new rival hotels opened nearby). items.stem: Based in Doha, Pearl Logistics WLL (private limited company) provides freight forwarding, warehousing and lorry delivery services. The business has around 1,500 employees. Large customers are asking for real-time tracking of every delivery. Analyse the likely impact on Pearl Logistics of a rise in unemployment in Qatar from 5% to 11%.
items.answer: Points to develop for Pearl Logistics: unemployment reduces household income and consumer confidence; lower demand for freight and warehousing services reduces revenue and capacity utilisation; a larger pool of job applicants makes recruitment easier and reduces wage pressure; staff morale may fall if employees fear redundancy.

items.stem: Based in Accra, Gold Coast Cocoa Ltd (private limited company) buys cocoa from local co-operatives and makes premium chocolate bars. The business has around 450 employees. World cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months. Discuss whether Gold Coast Cocoa should spend more time on strategic planning given how quickly its market is changing.
items.answer: For: direction and coordination; anticipates threats; allocates resources. Against: plans become out of date; emergent strategy may be better; cost of planning. Judgement: the decision for Gold Coast Cocoa depends mainly on the speed of change, and also on the quality of information.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts/theory. AO2 Application [2]: uses case evidence (Gold Coast Cocoa: confectionery, about 450 employees, private limited company in Ghana; world cocoa prices have doubled in eighteen months). AO3 Analysis [2]: arguments for, e.g. direction and coordination; anticipates threats; allocates resources; arguments against, e.g. plans become out of date; emergent strategy may be better; cost of planning. AO4 Evaluation [2]: a supported judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on the speed of change; the quality of information; the flexibility of the plan. Highest level needs a justified conclusion specific to Gold Coast Cocoa, not a generic one. [8]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Discuss whether lean production is suitable for all businesses such as Nusantara Apparel.
items.answer: For: cuts waste and costs; improves quality; more responsive. Against: needs stable demand and reliable suppliers; cultural change; vulnerable to shocks. Judgement: the decision for Nusantara Apparel depends mainly on its industry and supply chain, and also on its workforce skills.
